Summary of ask / context:
- Medica Health will evaluate Redwood for text generation and document ingestion use cases that may include limited PHI in clinical notes.
- Primary concerns: data retention, logging/audits, role-based access, encryption & key management, and SOC 2 evidence.

Proposed MAP milestone: Data handling & compliance (draft)
- Objective: Validate Redwood's controls and align on retention & logging policy for production pilot.
- Milestone owner (Redwood): Marissa Cole (SE) — technical evidence and configuration options.
- Milestone owner (Medica): Samantha Hales — security reviewer; Brian Lee — procurement/contract point.
- Deliverables: (1) configuration options doc + technical Q&A, (2) SOC 2 artifact checklist, (3) signed DPA + updated MAP.
- Target completion: 2026-12-10 (target close for milestone to unblock pilot).
- Dependencies: DPA execution, access to sample telemetry logs (read-only), and confirmation of PHI scope for pilot.

Next steps I propose:
1) Marissa to send a short technical note on retention/logging options and PHI handling points (by EOD 11/29).
2) Samantha to share SOC 2 artifact list and procurement cadence (if available).
3) Aditya to circulate updated MAP (v1.1) with clarified responsibilities and DocuSign link for DPA.

Thanks Aditya — appreciate the clear recap. A few quick clarifications from our security team after an initial read: 

1) PHI/PII scope: we need confirmation on whether any unredacted PHI may be persisted during inference or only in ephemeral cache. For the pilot we expect limited clinical notes with patient identifiers — we need options to ensure those identifiers are not retained beyond necessary.

2) Retention windows: what are your configurable retention windows for KV cache and telemetry/logs? Do you support customer-configured retention at the tenant level?

3) Audit trails: we need exportable audit logs showing who accessed what and when (for 90 days at a minimum). Is this baked into the hosted offering or only available in Private?

4) Encryption & keys: confirm whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production.

I've attached a short SOC 2 evidence request spreadsheet our team uses — please have Marissa review and indicate which artifacts you can produce. Also loop in procurement once we have the MAP and DPA language.

Subject: Re: MAP: Data handling & compliance - Technical note (retention, logging, PHI)

Hi Samantha — thanks for the clear list. Below is a concise mapping of Redwood's current capabilities and the options we can offer for the pilot. Happy to jump on a short call to walk through any item.

1) PHI/PII persistence
- Default behavior: request context and KV cache are ephemeral by default and not persisted beyond configured retention. Model outputs are generated in-memory; KV cache entries (prefix caching) are persisted per-tenant only if cache persistence is enabled.
- Pilot options:
  a) Ephemeral-only mode: disable cache persistence for the pilot so no PII/PHI is written to long-term storage. This is the safest quick option.
  b) Short retention: if caching improves latency for a defined workload, we can set cache retention to 24–72 hours and purge automatically.
  c) Redaction hooks: we provide pre-send redaction patterns to strip identifiers before they reach the model.

2) Retention windows (configurable)
- Telemetry/logs: default retention 90 days for hosted plan; we can configure shorter windows for pilot (e.g., 30 days) or longer for dedicated/private.
- KV cache and prompt storage: configurable per-tenant; options: ephemeral (session-only), 24/72/90 days, or custom retention on request.

3) Audit trails / logging
- We provide exportable audit logs with timestamped events (request id, user id, model used, route, token counts, response status). Logs can be exported via S3 or secure streaming to your SIEM.
- For hosted customers, full audit exports are available as part of the SOC 2 add-on; for Private deployments, audit collection is in-customer control and can be retained as required.

4) Encryption & KMS
- Encryption in transit and at rest (AES-256) is standard.
- Customer-managed keys: we support bringing your own keys via integrations with major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) for both Hosted and Dedicated; HSM-backed keys available for Private deployments.

5) Data access controls & RBAC
- Role-based access with SSO/SAML integration, fine-grained permissions for viewing/exporting logs and managing keys.
- Admin auditing available via console and log exports.

6) Evidence & artifacts
- We can provide SOC 2 Type II report (redacted), configuration screenshots, architecture diagrams, and a mapping spreadsheet for common evidence items. See attached: SOC 2 checklist (Aditya — reference Samantha's attachment)

Dependencies we flagged for the MAP milestone:
- Signed DPA (baseline for PHI scope and allowed processing).
- Confirmation from Medica on PHI fields and whether tokenization/redaction is acceptable pre-ingest.
- For KMS/HSM: exchange of key policies and egress requirements if Private is chosen.

Suggested updated MAP milestones & responsibilities (short):
- Tech Q&A and artifact delivery (Owner: Marissa) — due 2026-12-03
- DPA review & redlines (Owner: Samantha / Medica procurement) — due 2026-12-06
- Pilot config (ephemeral mode or short retention) + test ingest (Owner: Dev / Redwood infra) — due 2026-12-10
- Final signoff to start pilot (Owner: Brian + Samantha) — target 2026-12-12

If those dates work, Aditya — can you update the MAP and include the DPA/DocuSign link and HubSpot deal id? We will prepare the artifacts for the Tech Q&A deliverable.

Best,
